Invalid JSON when parsing {"candidates":[{"candidate_id":"cand-01-verifier-semantic-coverage","title":"Empirical measurement of deterministic verifier coverage for semantic/policy-level failures in LLM-generated network configurations","research_question":"To what extent do deterministic verifiers (syntax/schema/invariant checkers) detect semantic and policy-level failures (e.g., cross-device invariants, reachability violations, policy non-compliance) in LLM-generated device configurations for realistic NetOps intents?","hypotheses":["Deterministic verifiers will detect the majority of syntactic and schema errors but will miss a substantial fraction (>25%) of semantic/policy-level failures detectable via network replay/emulation.","Augmenting deterministic verification with a lightweight sandboxed reachability replay step will significantly reduce the semantic false-negative rate compared to verifier-only acceptance (expected absolute reduction >15%)."],"proposed_design":"Preregistered paired evaluation. Create a corpus of 300 natural-language NetOps intents (publicly-sourced templates and variations) mapped to 3× target topologies (small, medium, chained devices) implemented with containerized network emulation (Docker/Mininet-like). For each intent: (1) call an LLM (hosted-model API) to generate device-level configs using fixed prompt templates and seeds; (2) run deterministic verifiers (syntax, schema, configured invariants); (3) run sandboxed replay/emulation to test semantic properties (reachability, ACL/policy compliance, cross-device invariants); (4) if verifier or sandbox fails, record failure class and attempt automated repair script (one deterministic repair pass). Freeze prompts, verifier rules, seeds, and replay tests before execution. Compare verifier results vs sandbox ground truth to compute false-negative and false-positive rates. Public tooling, prompts, and corpus archived for reproducibility.","expected_data":"Per-sample records: intent id, prompt, model output, verifier-pass boolean, verifier-failure-type, sandbox-pass boolean, sandbox-failure-type (reachability/policy/invariant), timestamps, repair attempts and outcomes, hashes. Aggregate counts of verifier false negatives (verifier pass & sandbox fail), false positives (verifier fail & sandbox pass), repair success rates, per-topology and per-intent subgroup counts.","primary_outcome":"Semantic false-negative rate of deterministic verifiers (proportion of cases where verifier accepted but sandbox/emulation detected semantic/policy failure).","analysis_outline":"Compute point estimates and 95% confidence intervals for semantic false-negative rates overall and by topology size. Use McNemar's test for paired binary outcomes (verifier-only vs verifier+sandbox) to assess reduction in false negatives. Subgroup analysis by intent type with Bonferroni-adjusted exploratory comparisons. Report repair success conditional probabilities and analyze common failure modes qualitatively with stratified counts and example traces.","novelty_evidence_ids":["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899","https://openalex.org/W7126281064","https://openalex.org/W7166901862"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899","https://openalex.org/W4413757586","https://openalex.org/W7162044063"],"risks":["Emulator/sandbox overfitting)."],"estimated_model_calls":2400},{"candidate_id":"cand-02-workflow-benchmark-replay","title":"Design and evaluation of a contamination-resistant, workflow-centered benchmark for end-to-end agentic NetOps (Generate–Verify–Replay–Rollback)","research_question":"Can a reproducible benchmark that enforces generate–verify–high-fidelity-replay–rollback evaluation reliably differentiate agentic NetOps pipelines by operational assurance while resisting common dataset/model contamination issues?","hypotheses":["A benchmark combining deterministic verification, high-fidelity sandbox replay with rollback-aware scoring, and contamination-resistance procedures will produce consistent, reproducible ranking of end-to-end agentic pipelines with higher discriminatory power than token-level accuracy metrics.","Contamination-resistance procedures (explicit provenance filtering, held-out real-world configuration templates, and synthetic intent augmentation) will materially reduce apparent performance variance attributable to pretraining data leakage compared to an unfiltered benchmark.",""],"proposed_design":"Construct an open benchmark suite (public release): (1) curated intent bank (n=400) synthesized from public operator guides and intentionally held-out configuration templates to reduce contamination; (2) device configuration templates across vendor-simulated images hosted in containerized emulators (Docker); (3) a standardized GVR evaluation harness: LLM generation (frozen prompts/seeds), deterministic verifier module, sandboxed replay/test harness, rollback execution simulator, and reproducible scoring (safety-first: verifier failures penalized, sandbox failures penalized, successful rollback credited). Run three representative agentic pipelines (LLM-only, LLM+verifier, LLM+verifier+sandbox) and measure inter-run stability across 5 runs. Publish dataset, harness, and evaluation code. Predefine contamination-detection checks (provenance matching against public corpora) in preregistration.","expected_data":"Per-run and per-intent scores (verifier-status, sandbox-status, rollback-success), end-to-end assurance score, runtime, logs, provenance match flags, and reproducibility metrics (inter-run variance). Aggregate benchmark ranking stability and contamination indicators.","primary_outcome":"Benchmark discriminative power measured as normalized inter-pipeline score separation (effect size, Cohen's d) and reproducibility measured as inter-run coefficient of variation (CV) for pipeline scores.","analysis_outline":"Compute pairwise effect sizes (Cohen's d) between pipelines, bootstrapped 95% CIs for mean scores, and ANOVA for score differences. Compare contamination vs filtered subsets using paired t-tests and measure variance explained by provenance leakage using regression. Report reproducibility CV and Kendall's tau rank stability across runs.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W7162044063","https://openalex.org/W4400377739","https://openalex.org/W7166901862"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W7166901862","https://openalex.org/W7164234446","https://openalex.org/W4408167800"],"risks":["Residual contamination may remain despite filtering (threat to validity).","Dockerized emulation may not reproduce vendor-specific firmware behaviors (external validity).","Benchmark design choices (scoring weights) could bias results; requires transparent justification.","Resource limits (hosted-model API costs) may limit scale if many models are evaluated."],"estimated_model_calls":1800},{"candidate_id":"cand-03-adversarial-poisoning-and-defenses","title":"Quantifying the effect of prompt/document poisoning and malicious tool descriptions on agentic NetOps outputs and verifier-assisted defenses","research_question":"How vulnerable are LLM-driven NetOps pipelines to prompt/document poisoning and malicious tool-description attacks, and to what extent do deterministic verifiers and simple RAG-provenance defenses mitigate resulting unsafe misconfigurations?","hypotheses":["Injecting poisoned context (malicious device docs or tool descriptions) into retrieval/RAG or prompt context will significantly increase unsafe or noncompliant configuration outputs compared to clean context.","A defend-then-verify pipeline (source-trust scoring + deterministic verifier) will reduce unsafe outputs relative to undefended pipelines but will not eliminate them entirely; residual unsafe rate will remain non-zero and measurable (>5%)."],"proposed_design":"Controlled adversarial experiment. Build a set of 240 intent+context pairs. For each pair produce three context conditions: clean, poisoned-RAG (malicious inserted doc chunk that recommends unsafe change), and poisoned-tool (malicious tool-description returned by a simulated tool). For each condition, generate configs via fixed LLM calls (frozen prompts/seeds). Evaluate outputs with deterministic verifiers and sandbox replay to label unsafe outputs. Implement two defenses: provenance-based source-trust filtering (drop low-trust retrieved chunks) and verifier-enforced rejection. Measure attack success rate (unsafe outputs) and reduction under defenses. Record provenance traces and log evidence. Publicly archive poisoning artifacts and defense code.","expected_data":"Per-sample labels: condition, model output, provenance sources, verifier-pass, sandbox-pass, unsafe-class, defense-applied boolean, detection/rejection events, timestamps. Aggregate attack success rates, defense efficacy (absolute and relative reduction), and false positives introduced by defenses.","primary_outcome":"Attack success rate (proportion of unsafe/sandbox-failing configurations) under poisoned vs clean contexts, and absolute reduction in attack success rate due to defenses.","analysis_outline":"Estimate attack success rates with 95% CIs for each condition. Use paired comparisons (McNemar or paired-proportion z-test) between clean and poisoned conditions and between defended and undefended pipelines. Compute ROC-like curves for provenance-trust thresholds vs detection of poisoned-induced unsafe outputs. Qualitative taxonomy of successful poisoning vectors.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4404534210","10.20944/preprints202512.0913.v1","10.3390/electronics15102214"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4404782868","doi:10.2139/ssrn.6754899","https://openalex.org/W4413757586"],"risks":["Adversarial artifact generation may overfit to the specific LLM used (model-specific attack patterns).","Ethical concerns: publication of poisoning examples requires care to avoid misuse (mitigate via redaction/abstraction).","Hosted-model API rate limits or policy blocking of adversarial content may impede reproducibility."],"estimated_model_calls":3000},{"candidate_id":"cand-04-grounding-metrics-correlation","title":"Operational grounding metrics for RAG/tool-augmented NetOps agents and their correlation with end-to-end correctness","research_question":"Which quantitative grounding/evidence-trace metrics for RAG and tool-augmented NetOps agents best correlate with operational correctness (sandbox-passed configurations), and can such metrics be used as early assurance signals?","hypotheses":["Composite grounding metrics (source coverage, provenance diversity, tool-confirmation-score) will show a statistically significant positive correlation (Pearson r > 0.4) with sandbox-determined operational correctness.","A simple provenance-threshold rule derived from grounding metrics will achieve useful early-warning capability (precision > 0.75 for predicting sandbox failure) allowing prioritized human or automated verification.",""],"proposed_design":"Define and preregister a set of grounding metrics: (1) source-coverage (fraction of tokens supported by at least one retrieved source), (2) provenance-diversity (count of distinct trusted sources), (3) tool-confirmation-score (number of independent tool outputs that corroborate generated change), and (4) conflict-score (contradictory evidence count). Generate 500 LLM-produced configurations for diverse intents using RAG + tool calls. For each sample compute grounding metrics, run deterministic verifier and sandbox replay to label correctness. Use withheld holdout for deriving a simple threshold-based predictor. Publish metric definitions and code.","expected_data":"Per-sample grounding metrics, verifier status, sandbox pass/fail, provenance traces, tool outputs, timestamps. Correlation tables, ROC/precision-recall curves for threshold predictors, and holdout performance metrics.","primary_outcome":"Correlation coefficients between each grounding metric and sandbox pass/fail (operational correctness); AUC/precision-recall of grounding-metric-based early-warning predictor on holdout.","analysis_outline":"Compute Pearson and Spearman correlations with 95% CIs between grounding metrics and binary correctness. Fit logistic regression models and report AUC, precision@k, and calibration plots. Use nested cross-validation to select thresholds and report holdout precision/recall. Analyze metric importance and failure cases qualitatively.","novelty_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4404782868","10.20944/preprints202604.1820.v1","https://openalex.org/W4400377739"],"feasibility_evidence_ids":["https://openalex.org/W4404782868","https://openalex.org/W4413757586","https://openalex.org/W4408167800"],"risks":["Grounding metrics may correlate with correctness only for the evaluated model/pipeline (limited external validity).","Tool outputs used for confirmation may be themselves noisy, confounding correlations.","Designing trust/polarity rules for provenance requires careful normalization across sources."],"estimated_model_calls":1400}]} for TypeAdapter(CandidateSet); 2 validation errors for CandidateSet
